hints: Look first at what is missing in the IR spectrum above 3000 cm-1, since a broad dip there tells you about O-H groups.
Notice the very strong, sharp dip at about 1740 cm-1, which is characteristic of a C=O bond, combined with no broad O-H absorption.
Check which skeletal structures have molecular formulas that simplify to C2H4O and contain C=O but no O-H group.
walkthrough:
**Use the empirical formula to limit the molecular formula**

Think of empirical formula as the simplest ratio. Any candidate must have atoms in the ratio C:H:O = 2:4:1.

So $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ is allowed because it simplifies to $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$, but $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ is not.

**Check the IR for O-H**

A broad absorption at 3200 to 3600 cm-1 means alcohol O-H, and a very broad absorption at 2500 to 3000 cm-1 means carboxylic acid O-H.

Here transmittance stays near 100% in that region except for sharp C-H peaks just below 3000 cm-1. So there is no alcohol and no carboxylic acid.

**Check the IR for C=O**

There is a very strong, sharp dip at about 1740 cm-1. That is the classic C=O stretch.

$$\text{absorption at } \approx 1740 \text{ cm}^{-1} \rightarrow \text{C=O present}$$
So X contains C=O but no O-H. That points to an ester, aldehyde or ketone, not an acid or alcohol.

**Test the four skeletal formulas**

Option A is ethyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Its molecular formula is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$, which gives empirical $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$, and it has ester C=O with no O-H. Perfect match.

options.A: Ethyl ethanoate is an ester with formula C4H8O2, so empirical formula is C2H4O. Its IR shows ester C=O at about 1740 cm-1, C-H just below 3000 cm-1, and C-O at 1000 to 1300 cm-1, with no broad O-H. This matches the spectrum exactly.
options.B: This cyclic ester (a lactone) is C4H6O2, which simplifies to C2H3O, not C2H4O. Students who focus only on the C=O peak and forget to check hydrogen count are tempted by this.
options.C: This is HOCH2CH=CHCHO, formula C4H6O2, so empirical formula is C2H3O. It also contains an alcohol O-H and an aldehyde C-H, which would give a broad O-H band near 3300 cm-1 that is absent. Do not choose it just because it has C=O.
options.D: This hydroxyketone, CH3COCH(OH)CH3, is C4H8O2 so the empirical formula fits, but it contains an alcohol OH. It would show a broad O-H stretch at 3200 to 3600 cm-1, which is clearly missing from the spectrum.
